about: The declared model catalogue of spec section 10, one entry for each declared model of the families built so far. Each entry has the six parts that section 10 requires: model (equations, closures, geometry, conditions and the declared dimensionless form), domain (parameters and assumptions), operations (symbolic and numerical), methods (the four analyses, each with the reason it applies or not) with limitations, acceptance (standard example, reference and tolerance) and solver (method, discretization, convergence and reproducibility). A record names its declared model in purpose.declaration; the page checks the Nondimensionalizer's result against the declared dimensionless form exactly.

declarations.title: Lumped body with convection

model.summary: A body whose temperature stays uniform, with heat capacity ρc_pV, cooled through its surface A_s by convection to a fluid at T_∞.

roles.meaning: conductivity of the body, for the Biot number

closures: Newton's law of cooling with constant h: the heat flow out of the surface is hA_s(T − T_∞).
model.geometry: Any shape. The Biot length is L_c = V/A_s. The comparison with a spatial model uses the shape in the record's geometry: a slab, a long cylinder, a sphere or a cube (the product of three slab solutions).

assumptions.text: The temperature is uniform in the body at each time. The comparison with the spatial model tests this assumption.
ρ, c_p, h and T_∞ are constant.
T_i is not equal to T_∞.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_τ = −θ and θ(0) = 1 with τ = t/(ρc_pV/(hA_s)).
The exact solution θ = e^{−τ}, checked in canonical form: ∂_τ e^{−τ} + e^{−τ} = 0.
The lumped model as the leading order of the small-Bi expansion of the spatial model (src/asymptotic.js).
numerical: The error of the lumped model against the spatial model of the declared shape, at each point of the map.
The decay time ρc_pV/(hA_s) and the temperature at the record's time.

dominant-balance.reason: The uniform-temperature assumption is a balance: the internal temperature drop is small compared with the drop across the surface film when Bi_c is small.

asymptotic.reason: The lumped model is the leading order of the outer expansion of the spatial model as Bi → 0 with the slow time fixed: a coupled limit.

stability.reason: The model is linear with one steady state θ = 0, and θ = e^{−τ} decays. A stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: The spatial comparison covers a slab, a long cylinder, a sphere and a cube. Other shapes need a separate declaration of the spatial model.
Radiation exchange makes the model nonlinear: piece 4 declares the lumped body with radiation.

acceptance.reference: θ = e^{−τ} (exact) and the decay time ρc_pV/(hA_s) from the record's values (exact). Also the lumped error against the page's slab series at Bi = 0.01, 0.001 and 0.0001 with Bi·Fo = 1.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the decay time and the solution. The lumped error must fall with Bi and be below 1e-3 at Bi = 10⁻⁴.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and condition equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The decay time from the record's values is exact, and θ = e^{−τ} solves θ_τ = −θ with θ(0) = 1 (exact).
The lumped error against the spatial model goes to 0 as Bi_c goes to 0 at a fixed Bi_c·Fo_c.

solver.method: Closed form θ = e^{−τ}. The spatial comparison uses the series of the declared shape (transient conduction declarations).
solver.discretization: None for the lumped model. The comparison uses 21 points in X for the slab, the cylinder and the sphere, and 21 × 21 × 21 points in an octant of the cube.
solver.convergence: The same mode count rule as the transient conduction declarations: λ_n²τ ≤ 50.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. Exact rationals for the decay time.

declarations.title: Transient conduction in a slab with surface convection

model.summary: A slab of half-thickness L with constant properties, uniform initial temperature T_i and convection to a fluid at T_∞ on its surface.
closures: The equation contains Fourier's law with constant k: q = −k ∂T/∂x.
model.geometry: A slab of half-thickness L, symmetric about its centre plane x = 0. Both faces see the same fluid.

conditions.meaning: convection to the fluid (Newton's law of cooling)

assumptions.text: The density, the specific heat capacity and the conductivity are constant.
h and T_∞ are constant and the same on all of the surface.
The initial temperature is uniform, and T_i is not equal to T_∞.
Heat flows in x only: the slab is wide compared with its thickness.
There is no heat source in the solid, and radiation is part of h or absent.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared dimensionless equation and conditions (canonical forms).

The small-Bi outer expansion to order 2 in exact rationals, with the solvability condition and the matching constant of each order. The residual is of order Bi³. The cross-check of C₁ and λ₁² goes to order 3.
Exact checks of the expansion: each order satisfies its equation, its surface condition and its solvability condition.
numerical: The exact series of modes cos(λX) with eigenvalues from Brent's method.
The one-mode, lumped, first-order outer, surface-temperature and short-time approximations, and their error at each point of the map.
The energy balance d(mean θ)/dτ = −(j + 1) Bi θ(1, τ) at the inspected point.

dominant-balance.reason: The surface condition compares conduction inside the solid with exchange at the surface (Bi). The equation compares the penetration depth with the size of the solid (Fo).

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 at fixed Bi·Fo gives the lumped model as the leading order of an outer expansion with an initial layer. Bi → ∞ gives the surface-temperature model, and Fo → 0 gives an inner region at the surface.

stability.reason: The model is linear with a unique steady state θ = 0. Each mode decays at the rate λ_n², so a stability analysis adds nothing.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so it has one solution for each Bi. No branch can split.

limitations: Constant properties only. A conductivity that changes with temperature needs a separate declaration.
Uniform h and T_∞. A surface condition that changes along the surface needs a 2D or 3D declaration.

The map uses the declared domain 0.001 ≤ Bi ≤ 1000 and 0.001 ≤ Fo ≤ 10. Where the series needs more than 400 modes, or the temperature excess is below 10⁻¹² of its initial value, the page shows an unresolved region.

acceptance.reference: The first six eigenvalues and coefficients for Bi = 0.1, 1, 10 and ∞, from mpmath with 30 digits. Also θ at the centre, the middle and the surface at Fo = 0.01, 0.1, 0.5 and 2 for Bi = 0.1, 1 and 10 (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-9 relative for the eigenvalues and coefficients, 1e-9 absolute for θ.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The eigenvalues, coefficients and temperatures agree with the mpmath reference within the tolerance.
The series gives θ = 1 inside the solid at the earliest time of the map, within 1e-9 at X ≤ 0.5.
The small-Bi expansion gives C₁ and λ₁² to order 3 exactly as SymPy's series of the eigenvalue equation.
The energy balance holds at the example's point within 1e-9.

solver.method: Separation of variables: θ = Σ C_n f_n(λ_nX) exp(−λ_n²τ).
solver.discretization: No mesh. The error measures use 21 equally spaced points X = 0, 0.05, …, 1.
solver.convergence: The series keeps the modes with λ_n²τ ≤ 50, so the first mode left out is below e⁻⁵⁰ times its coefficient. At most 400 modes. Each eigenvalue has its own bracket, and Brent's method stops at 1e-15.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. The same inputs give the same numbers on every run. Reference values: mpmath 1.3.0 with 30 digits.

declarations.title: Slab with a uniform heat source, steady state

model.summary: A slab of half-thickness L with a uniform volumetric heat source q_v, cooled by convection on both faces. Steady state, constant properties.

roles.meaning: reference temperature difference, such as the allowed rise

closures: Fourier's law with constant k.
model.geometry: A slab of half-thickness L, symmetric about x = 0, with the same fluid on both faces.

assumptions.text: The source q_v, the conductivity, h and T_∞ are constant.
The slab is at steady state.
ΔT is a positive reference scale, such as the allowed temperature rise.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_XX + Γ = 0 with the declared conditions.
The exact solution θ = Γ(1 − X²)/2 + Γ/Bi in rationals, the heat balance Γ = Bi θ(1), and the exact approximation boundaries.
numerical: None: every value is an exact rational when the inputs are rational.

dominant-balance.reason: The internal temperature drop Γ/2 and the surface excess Γ/Bi compete. Their ratio is Bi/2 exactly.

asymptotic.reason: Bi → 0 gives a uniform temperature and Bi → ∞ gives a prescribed surface temperature. Each expansion stops after two terms, so each two-term result is exact.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution. A stability analysis needs the transient model and adds nothing for a constant source.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: Steady state only. The declaration of the transient slab gives the time history without a source.
A source that depends on temperature, such as a reaction, makes the model nonlinear and needs a separate declaration.

acceptance.reference: θ = Γ(1 − X²)/2 + Γ/Bi (exact, in rationals) and its heat balance. SymPy solves the same boundary-value problem (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact: rational equality.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The solution satisfies the equation and both conditions exactly, and SymPy gives the same polynomial.
The heat balance: the source Γ leaves through the surface as Bi θ(1) (exact).
The balance crossover is at Bi = 2 exactly.

solver.method: Closed form, exact rational arithmetic (BigInt).
solver.discretization: None.
solver.convergence: None needed: the solution is exact.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals give the same digits on every machine.

declarations.title: Two-layer plane wall with a contact resistance

model.summary: Two plane layers in series with a thermal contact resistance R_c between them, convection to a fluid on each face, steady state.
closures: Fourier's law with a constant conductivity in each layer.
The contact resistance: the heat flux across the interface is (T_1 − T_2)/R_c.
model.geometry: Layer 1 on 0 < x < L_1 and layer 2 on L_1 < x < L_1 + L_2. Face 1 is at x = 0 and face 2 at x = L_1 + L_2.

conditions.meaning: the temperature jump across the contact resistance

parameters.meaning: contact resistance in units of the resistance of layer 1
Biot number of face 2, with L_1 and k_1

assumptions.text: Steady state and constant properties in each layer.
Heat flows in x only: the wall is wide compared with its thickness.
The thermal contact resistance R_c is a declared input per unit area. It is not a mechanical contact model.
T_∞1 is not equal to T_∞2.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared equations and the four conditions.
The exact solution in rationals: the series resistances, the heat flux, every interface temperature and the jump across the contact.
Exact checks: the heat flux is the same in each layer and through the contact, and the temperatures close at fluid 2.
The resistance limits r_c → 0 (perfect contact) and r_c → ∞ (the contact takes all of the temperature difference), with exact error formulas.
numerical: The map evaluates the exact formulas in double precision.

dominant-balance.reason: The temperature drop across each element is the heat flux times its resistance, so the largest resistance controls the heat flow.

asymptotic.reason: r_c → 0 and r_c → ∞ are regular limits of the exact solution. Each has a convergent series, in r_c/R₀ or in R₀/r_c.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: The record match accepts two layers only. The resistance sum also applies to more layers.
Mechanical contact (pressure, roughness) needs a separate structural declaration. R_c is an input here.

acceptance.reference: The resistance sum, heat flux and interface temperatures in exact rationals, and SymPy's solution of the same linear system (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact: rational equality.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equations and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The heat flux is the same in each layer and through the contact (exact).
The temperature jump across the contact is q R_c (exact), and the temperatures close at fluid 2 (exact).
SymPy's solution of the linear system gives the same heat flux and temperatures.

solver.method: Series thermal resistances in exact rationals.
solver.discretization: None.
solver.convergence: None needed.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals give the same digits on every machine.

declarations.title: Straight fin of constant cross-section

model.summary: A straight fin of length L, cross-section A_c and exposed perimeter P, with uniform convection h, a prescribed base temperature and an insulated or convective tip.
closures: Fourier's law along the fin with constant k, and Newton's law of cooling on the sides with constant h.
model.geometry: A straight fin with constant A_c and P. x runs from the base (x = 0) to the tip (x = L).

alternatives.meaning: a convective tip with the same h

parameters.meaning: fin parameter mL, with m² = hP/(kA_c)
tip Biot number hL/k (0 for an insulated tip)

assumptions.text: Constant conductivity, uniform h and a prescribed base temperature.
The temperature varies along x only. The transverse validity condition needs its own derivation, which the dominant-balance step gives.
ΔT = T_b − T_∞ is not 0.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_XX − λ²θ = 0, θ(0) = 1 and the tip condition.
The small-λ expansion to order λ⁸ in exact rationals, with each order checked against its equation and conditions.
The large-λ boundary layer at the base and its matching to the outer solution θ = 0.
numerical: θ(X) = cosh(λ(1 − X))/cosh λ for the insulated tip, Q̇L/(kA_cΔT) = λ tanh λ and η_f = tanh λ/λ, written with e^{−λ} so that no value overflows.
The base heat flow against the total heat loss of the surface, by Gauss–Legendre quadrature.

dominant-balance.reason: Conduction along the fin and loss through the surface compete through λ². Conduction across the fin and loss at the surface compete through the transverse Biot number hA_c/(kP).

asymptotic.reason: λ → 0 is a regular expansion in λ². λ → ∞ loses the second derivative in the outer region, so a boundary layer of thickness 1/λ forms at the base.

stability.reason: The steady linear model has one solution.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear, so no branch can split.

limitations: Constant cross-section only. A tapered or annular fin needs a separate declaration.
The 1D model does not establish the transverse condition hA_c/(kP) ≪ 1. The page shows that estimate as a separate balance.

acceptance.reference: λ tanh λ, tanh λ/λ and the profile at λ = √(11/32) from mpmath with 30 digits, and the Taylor series of λ tanh λ from SymPy (tools/references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-12 relative for the heat flow and the profile. Exact for the series coefficients.
checks: The Nondimensionalizer's equation and conditions equal the declared dimensionless model (exact).
The base heat flow, the efficiency and the profile agree with mpmath within the tolerance.
The base heat flow equals the total heat loss of the surface within 1e-12.
The small-λ expansion gives the Taylor coefficients of λ tanh λ exactly.

solver.method: Closed form with exponentials: θ = [(1 + β)e^{−λX} + (1 − β)e^{−λ(2 − X)}]/[(1 + β) + (1 − β)e^{−2λ}], β = Bi_t/λ.
solver.discretization: None. The heat-balance check uses 8 panels of the 20-point Gauss–Legendre rule.
solver.convergence: None needed for the closed form.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision.

declarations.title: Boussinesq layer in a box heated from below

model.summary: A two-dimensional cell of depth H and width L lies between no-slip isothermal plates at T_h (below) and T_c (above). It has stress-free adiabatic side walls and follows the Boussinesq approximation. The stream function ψ and the vorticity ω describe the flow. The box holds exactly the mirror-symmetric rolls of a periodic layer of period 2L.

equations.text: d(omega,t) + d(psi,z)*d(omega,x) - d(psi,x)*d(omega,z) = nu*(d(omega,x,x) + d(omega,z,z)) - g*beta*d(T,x)

closures: Boussinesq: the density changes only in the buoyancy term, ρ = ρ_0[1 − β(T − T_c)].
Newtonian viscosity and Fourier conduction with constant ν and κ.
u = ∂ψ/∂z, w = −∂ψ/∂x, so the flow is incompressible.
model.geometry: A two-dimensional cell 0 < x < L, 0 < z < H. Γ = L/H. The plates are horizontal. Gravity points down, in the direction −z.

conditions.meaning: no flow through the lower plate
no slip at the lower plate
no flow through the upper plate
no slip at the upper plate
no flow through the left wall
no shear stress at the left wall
no flow through the right wall
no shear stress at the right wall

equations.text: d(Omega,tau) + d(Psi,Z)*d(Omega,X) - d(Psi,X)*d(Omega,Z) = Pr*(d(Omega,X,X) + d(Omega,Z,Z)) - Pr*Ra*d(theta,X)

symmetry.text: the reflection X → Γ − X with Ψ → −Ψ and Ω → −Ω

assumptions.text: The Boussinesq approximation applies: βΔT ≪ 1, and the properties are constant.
The flow is two-dimensional. With stress-free adiabatic side walls, the box holds exactly the mirror-symmetric rolls of a periodic layer of period 2L.
The plates are no-slip and isothermal, as in Wen, Goluskin and Doering (2022).

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared equations and the 14 conditions.
Exact check of the conductive base state θ = 1 − Z, Ψ = Ω = 0 in every equation and condition.
Exact perturbation equations: the order-ε part of the substitution.
Exact check of the reflection symmetry X → Γ − X, Ψ → −Ψ, Ω → −Ω.
numerical: Growth rates σ of each box mode a = nπ/Γ, with the eigenmode and its residual.
The neutral curve Ra(a) of the unbounded layer and its minimum (Ra_c, a_c).
The steady roll branch by Newton's method and continuation in Ra, with Nu, Re and a resolution check.
The amplitude equation at onset, and the stability of the rolls to disturbances of the same period and symmetry.

dominant-balance.reason: At onset, viscous diffusion balances the buoyancy torque. The advection terms are of second order in the amplitude.

asymptotic.reason: The weakly nonlinear expansion in ε = Ra/Ra_c − 1 gives the amplitude equation of the rolls.

stability.reason: The conductive state is a steady solution. Convection starts where the conductive state becomes linearly unstable in time.

bifurcation.reason: Rolls branch from the conductive state at onset. Continuation follows the branch, and the amplitude equation classifies the pitchfork.

limitations: Two-dimensional states in the box only. Three-dimensional convection, turbulence and the cavity heated from the side need separate declarations.
Stress-free adiabatic side walls are an idealization. With rigid side walls the onset is at a higher Ra.
The acceptance test validates the roll branch for Ra ≤ 10⁴ against Wen, Goluskin and Doering (2022) at Pr = 1. The page does not compute it above 10⁴.
Stability of the rolls covers disturbances of the same period and mirror symmetry only.

acceptance.reference: Ra_c and a_c of the unbounded layer from the independent SciPy script (tools/stability_references.py), and Ra_c ≈ 1708 with the period 2.016 (Wen, Goluskin and Doering 2022). Nu of steady rolls at Pr = 1 and period 2 from their Table 1S, at 15 values of Ra up to 10⁴.
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-7 relative for Ra_c, 1e-4 for a_c, 1e-4 relative for Nu, 1e-5 relative between two resolutions.
checks: Ra_c converges between 16 and 24 nodes.
Ra_c and a_c agree with the SciPy reference.
At the critical point the largest growth rate is real and 0.
Nu of the roll branch agrees with Table 1S.
Nu at Ra = 10⁴ converges in the resolution.
The amplitude equation gives a supercritical pitchfork.

solver.method: Chebyshev collocation in z on a basis that meets the wall conditions, W = (1 − ξ²)²p and Θ = (1 − ξ²)q, Thus each eigenproblem is standard. Hessenberg QR gives the eigenvalues. The rolls use Fourier modes in x (ψ odd, θ even), Newton's method and continuation in Ra. A Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction of the discrete system gives the stationary amplitude equation.
solver.discretization: 16 interior nodes for the linear analysis and 14 for the map. 8 Fourier modes × 16 nodes for the rolls, with 32 points in x for the products.
solver.convergence: Ra_c to 1e-9 between 16 and 24 nodes. Nu to 1e-5 between 8 × 16 and 10 × 20. Newton stops at a row-scaled residual of 1e-11.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. The reference script pins NumPy and SciPy.

declarations.title: Lumped body with grey radiation to an enclosure

model.summary: A body has a uniform temperature, the heat capacity ρc_pV and the surface A_s with the emissivity ε. It receives the heat Q and exchanges grey radiation with a large enclosure at T_e.

roles.meaning: conductivity of the body, for the radiation Biot number

closures: Grey diffuse exchange of a small body with a large enclosure: the net loss is εσA_s(T⁴ − T_e⁴) (Lienhard, section 10.4).
model.geometry: Any shape that is small compared with the enclosure. The radiation Biot number uses L_c = V/A_s.

parameters.meaning: supplied heat over the enclosure emission

assumptions.text: The temperature is uniform in the body: the radiation Biot number stays below 0.1 (Lienhard, section 1.3).
The surface is grey and diffuse, and the enclosure is large and at a uniform T_e.
Temperatures are absolute.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ_τ = q + 1 − θ⁴ and θ(0) = θ_i.
Exact perturbation equation and the exact derivative f′(θ) = −4θ³.
numerical: The equilibrium (1 + q)^{1/4}, the closed-form transient by Brent's method, and a Dormand–Prince check.
The error of the linearized decay and of the emission-only model at each point of the map.

dominant-balance.reason: Emission θ⁴ balances absorption and supply 1 + q. Far above the equilibrium, emission controls the heat loss.

asymptotic.reason: Near the equilibrium a regular expansion in θ_i − θ* gives the linearized decay with h_rad = 4εσT_e³θ*³.

stability.reason: The equilibrium is a steady state. Its eigenvalue −4θ*³ gives linear stability, and the balance decreases strictly, so the equilibrium attracts every start with θ_i > 0.

bifurcation.reason: f(θ) = q + 1 − θ⁴ decreases strictly for θ > 0. Thus the one equilibrium stays stable, and no branch splits.

limitations: Uniform temperature only: a large radiation Biot number needs a spatial model.
A grey diffuse surface and a large isothermal enclosure only. View factors to a finite enclosure need the surface-radiation model.

acceptance.reference: The equilibrium (1 + q)^{1/4} and the closed form τ = G(θ_i) − G(θ), with G(θ) = ln|(θ − a)/(θ + a)|/(4a³) − arctan(θ/a)/(2a³). An mpmath integration checks it (tools/stability_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-12 for the equilibrium, 1e-8 for the transient.
checks: The equilibrium satisfies the balance.
The closed form agrees with the Dormand–Prince integration.
The eigenvalue −4θ*³ is negative.

solver.method: Closed form for the transient (Brent's method on G), and the Dormand–Prince 5(4) integrator as a check.
solver.discretization: None for the closed form. The map has 41 × 31 points.
solver.convergence: Brent to 1e-15. Dormand–Prince with rtol 1e-11 and atol 1e-13.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision.

declarations.title: Grey duct with adiabatic side walls

model.summary: A long duct has a grey floor 1 at T_1, a grey ceiling 2 at T_2 and adiabatic side walls R. The side walls reradiate all that they absorb. The radiosity balance of each surface gives the net exchange.

roles.meaning: view factor from the floor to the ceiling
view factor from the floor to the side walls
net radiative flux of the floor

closures: Grey diffuse surfaces with uniform radiosity on each surface (Lienhard, section 10.4).
Floor and ceiling have the same width, so F_21 = F_12, F_2R = F_1R and F_R1 = F_R2.
model.geometry: A long duct of width W and height H. The crossed-string rule gives F_12 = (√(W² + H²) − H)/W (Lienhard, problem 10.14). The record gives the width W and the height H.

parameters.meaning: view factor from the floor to the ceiling

assumptions.text: Grey diffuse surfaces, each with a uniform temperature and radiosity.
The side walls are adiabatic: they reradiate all that they absorb.
The duct is long, so the end walls do not take part (two-dimensional view factors).

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives the declared radiosity balances.
Exact crossed-string view factors, reciprocity and summation for a rational √(W² + H²).
The exact rational solution of the network, its closed form and the energy balance.
numerical: The error of the black-surface model at each point of the map, and the dimensional flux with σ.

dominant-balance.reason: The page compares the surface resistances of the network with its space resistance, as exact ratios.

asymptotic.reason: The network is linear and has a closed form, so the page needs no expansion.

stability.reason: The model is a steady linear network in the radiosities, with no time derivative.

bifurcation.reason: The network is linear and nonsingular, so its solution is unique and no branch splits.

limitations: Two-dimensional view factors of a long duct. Finite ducts and other shapes need their own view factors.
Grey diffuse surfaces only. Spectral or specular surfaces need a separate declaration.
No medium between the surfaces absorbs radiation. Radiation in a medium is a piece 8 family.

acceptance.reference: Exact rationals from SymPy (tools/stability_references.py). F_12 = 1/2, F_1R = 1/2 and F_R1 = 1/3 for W = 4, H = 3. The net flux q_1/(σT_1⁴) = 45/124 for ε_1 = 4/5, ε_2 = 1/2, T_2/T_1 = 1/2.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact.
checks: Crossed-string view factors, reciprocity and summation.
The radiosity solution equals the closed form of the network.
The floor gives what the ceiling takes.

solver.method: Exact Gaussian elimination in rationals (src/linalg.js) for the network. The closed form for the map.
solver.discretization: None.
solver.convergence: None needed.
solver.reproducibility: BigInt rationals. The map uses double precision.

declarations.title: Surface with a supplied flux, convection and radiation

model.summary: A surface receives the heat flux q_s. It loses heat by convection with h to a fluid at T_∞, and by grey radiation to surroundings at T_∞.

roles.meaning: temperature of the fluid and the surroundings

closures: Newton's law of cooling with constant h.
Grey exchange with large surroundings at T_∞ (Lienhard, section 2.3).
model.geometry: A flat surface. The balance is per unit area.

assumptions.text: h is constant and does not depend on the temperature.
The surroundings are large and at the fluid temperature T_∞.
Temperatures are absolute.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives Q = θ − 1 + N_r(θ⁴ − 1).
The exact derivative dQ/dθ = 1 + 4N_rθ³ > 0 and the exact identity T⁴ − T_∞⁴ = 4T_m³ΔT[1 + (ΔT/2T_m)²].
numerical: The root θ by Brent's method, and the errors of the linearized and mean-temperature models at each point of the map.

dominant-balance.reason: Radiation and convection are of the same order when N_r(θ⁴ − 1) is near θ − 1. The ratio of the two fluxes is exact at the solution.

asymptotic.reason: A regular expansion in Q gives the linearization limit θ − 1 = Q/(1 + 4N_r).

stability.reason: The balance is steady and algebraic. It has one root, because the loss increases monotonically with θ.

bifurcation.reason: The root is unique for every Q > 0, so no branch splits.

limitations: Constant h: a temperature-dependent natural-convection coefficient needs a correlation (piece 7).
Surroundings at the fluid temperature. Other surroundings need a separate temperature ratio.

acceptance.reference: The root of the full balance by Brent's method, checked against mpmath (tools/stability_references.py), and the linearization limit.
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-12 for the root.
checks: The root satisfies the full balance.
The linearization error goes to 0 like Q.

solver.method: Brent's method on the monotone balance.
solver.discretization: None. The map has 41 × 31 points.
solver.convergence: Brent to 1e-15.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision.

declarations.title: Euler column with pinned ends (anchor test 4)

model.summary: A straight prismatic column of length L and bending stiffness EI carries the axial compressive load P between two pins. The linear eigenvalue problem gives the critical load and the buckling modes.
closures: Euler–Bernoulli bending: the moment is M = −EI w'', and the axial load is constant along the column (MIT 16.01 Unified Engineering, materials and structures handout).
model.geometry: A straight column of constant cross-section, coordinate x from one pin (x = 0) to the other (x = L).

conditions.meaning: no deflection at the first support
no bending moment at the first support
no deflection at the second support
no bending moment at the second support

assumptions.text: Small deflections and slopes: the curvature is w''.
No shear deformation: plane sections stay normal to the axis.
The load is axial and constant: a dead load.

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives W'''' + λW'' = 0 with the four pinned conditions.
Exact check of the modes sin(nπX) with λ = n²π², in rational multiples of powers of π.
numerical: Hermite cubic finite elements: the generalized eigenproblem K v = λ G v by a Cholesky factor and Jacobi rotations.
Mesh convergence on 4, 8, 16 and 32 elements.

dominant-balance.reason: The model has one balance, bending against the moment of the axial load, and it holds at every buckling mode. No term is small, so there is no term to neglect.

asymptotic.reason: The linear model has no small parameter. The slenderness that justifies it is an assumption of the declaration, not a computed limit.

stability.reason: The straight state is stable below the smallest eigenvalue λ = π² and not stable above it. This is a linear static stability analysis whose neutral condition is the smallest eigenvalue of the buckling problem.

bifurcation.reason: The linear eigenproblem fixes the mode shape but not its amplitude, so it cannot classify the branch. The declared model elastica (nonlinear buckling) does this.

limitations: The linear model gives no deflection after buckling and no amplitude of the mode.
Pinned ends only; clamped and free ends need their own declarations.
No shear deformation, no plasticity and no contact: each needs a separate declaration.

acceptance.reference: λ_cr = π² and the mode sin(πX) (MIT 16.01 Unified Engineering, materials and structures handout). mpmath gives π² to 30 digits (tools/structures_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the closed-form modes; 1e-6 relative for the element solution on 32 elements.
checks: The modes sin(nπX) with λ = n²π² satisfy the equation and the four conditions exactly.
The element solution gives λ_cr within 1e-6 of π².
The element error falls at an order above 3.5.

solver.method: Hermite cubic beam elements; K v = λ G v by a Cholesky factor of G and cyclic Jacobi rotations.
solver.discretization: 4, 8, 16 and 32 equal elements.
solver.convergence: Jacobi off-diagonal norm below 1e-13 of the diagonal norm; observed order of the eigenvalue error above 3.5.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision, no random numbers.

declarations.title: Simply supported beam under a uniform load and an axial load

model.summary: A straight prismatic beam of span L on two simple supports carries the uniform load q and the axial compression P. Without P it is the classical beam; P amplifies the deflection.
closures: Euler–Bernoulli bending, M = −EI w''; the load q is uniform.
model.geometry: A straight beam of constant cross-section, coordinate x from one support (x = 0) to the other (x = L).

conditions.meaning: no deflection at the first support
no bending moment at the first support
no deflection at the second support
no bending moment at the second support

assumptions.text: Small deflections and slopes; no shear deformation.
The axial load is below the critical load π²EI/L², so the straight beam is stable.

symbolic: Exact polynomial solution W = (X − 2X³ + X⁴)/24 for λ = 0, checked in rationals.
Closed form for λ > 0 with its series near λ = 0.
numerical: Hermite cubic elements with the consistent load: nodal values.
The midspan deflection of the closed form on the map.

dominant-balance.reason: For a small λ the bending term carries the load and the axial term is a small correction; the ratio λ/π² measures the axial term.

asymptotic.reason: The first sine term of the deflection gives the amplification factor 1/(1 − λ/π²). A regular expansion in λ gives 5/384 + 61λ/46080.

stability.reason: The straight beam is stable for λ < π², the critical load of the pinned column.

bifurcation.reason: With the transverse load q there is no symmetric straight state, so no branch splits. The deflection grows without bound as λ → π².

limitations: Uniform load and pinned ends only.
Linear: valid for small deflections; no post-buckling state.

acceptance.reference: W(1/2) = 5/384 for λ = 0 (the classical 5qL⁴/(384EI)); SymPy computes the exact polynomial (tools/structures_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for λ = 0; 1e-12 absolute for the element nodal values.
checks: W(X) = (X − 2X³ + X⁴)/24 satisfies W'''' = 1 and the four conditions exactly.
W(1/2) = 5/384 exactly.
Hermite elements give the exact nodal deflections.

solver.method: Closed form: exact polynomial for λ = 0, and W(1/2) = (sec(√λ/2) − 1)/λ² − 1/(8λ) for λ > 0 (a series below λ = 10⁻³).
solver.discretization: Hermite cubic elements, 2, 4 and 8 elements, as a check. The map has 161 points.
solver.convergence: Nodal values exact up to rounding.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript; rational arithmetic for λ = 0.

declarations.title: Elastica: perfect and eccentric pinned column

model.summary: An inextensible elastic column of length L has pinned ends. The load P acts on a line at the distance e from the ends; e = 0 is the perfect column. The angle θ(s) of the axis obeys the nonlinear elastica equation.
closures: The moment is EI times the curvature dθ/ds for any rotation (the Euler elastica: no stretch and no shear).
model.geometry: Arc length s from one end (s = 0) to the other (s = L). The load acts on the line through two points at the distance e from the ends.

conditions.meaning: the end moment of the eccentric load at the first end
the end moment of the eccentric load at the second end

assumptions.text: The column does not stretch and does not shear (the elastica).
Linear elastic moment–curvature law at any rotation.
Dead load; the first-mode branch, with θ(L − s) = −θ(s).

symbolic: Exact check that the Nondimensionalizer gives θ'' + λ sin θ = 0 with θ' = λê at both ends.
Exact symmetry θ → −θ of the perfect model, and the exact series λ/π² = 1 + θ0²/8 + … in rational arithmetic.
numerical: RK4 shooting with the variational equations, Newton's method and pseudo-arclength continuation in (θ0, λ).
Branch points by bisection of ∂R/∂θ0 on θ = 0; stability by the eigenvalues of the second variation with the end constraint.

dominant-balance.reason: The model has one balance, bending against the moment of the load, at every point of the branch. No term is small along the branch.

asymptotic.reason: Near the branch point a regular expansion in θ0 gives λ/π² = 1 + θ0²/8 + …; for a small eccentricity and λ < π² the linear (secant) theory is the first term.

stability.reason: Static stability under the dead load: the sign of the smallest eigenvalue of the second variation of the energy, with the constraint that the ends stay on the load line.

bifurcation.reason: The perfect column has a branch point at λ = π². The symmetry θ → −θ and the positive series coefficient 1/8 classify it as a supercritical pitchfork. The eccentricity removes the branch point.

limitations: First-mode branch only; the page does not follow the branches from the higher branch points, or search for disconnected branches.
Dead load and pinned ends only.
No stretch, no shear, no plasticity: each needs a separate declaration.

acceptance.reference: λ = 4K(m)² with the parameter m = sin²(θ0/2) for the perfect pinned elastica, from Λ = 2K for mode one (Holmes 2019; mpmath, 30 digits), and SciPy solve_bvp for the eccentric column (tools/structures_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-7 relative in λ for the perfect branch; 1e-6 in θ0 for the eccentric branch.
checks: The first branch point is λ = π² within 1e-6.
Shooting agrees with 4K² at six end rotations.
The series coefficient of θ0² is exactly 1/8.
The eccentric branch agrees with SciPy.

solver.method: Shooting from s = 0 with RK4 and the variational equations; Newton's method; pseudo-arclength continuation; bisection for branch points.
solver.discretization: 200 RK4 steps; 50 intervals for the second variation.
solver.convergence: Newton to 1e-12; observed RK4 order above 3.5 at 50 to 400 steps.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision. The perfect branch starts at θ0 = ±0.02 near λ = π². The eccentric branch starts at λ = 0.1π².

declarations.title: Damped oscillator under a harmonic force

model.summary: A force F_0 cos(Ωt) drives a mass m on a linear spring k and a linear damper c. The mass starts from rest.
closures: Linear spring force ku and linear damper force c du/dt.
model.geometry: One degree of freedom; time t only.

assumptions.text: The spring and the damper are linear.

symbolic: Exact check of the dimensionless equation and the initial conditions.
The steady solution A cos rτ + B sin rτ and the energy balance B = 2ζr(A² + B²), exact in rationals when r and ζ are rational.
numerical: RK4 from rest until the transient decays below 1e-10, with the cosine and sine parts of the last period.
The amplitude ratio at each point of the map.

dominant-balance.reason: For r ≪ 1 the spring term carries the force (|H| → 1); for r ≫ 1 the inertia term does (|H| ≈ 1/r²); near r = 1 the damper balances the force.

asymptotic.reason: The limits r → 0 and r → ∞ at fixed ζ give the quasi-static and the inertia-controlled responses; the undamped response is the limit ζ → 0 away from r = 1.

stability.reason: Both roots of s² + 2ζs + 1 have a negative real part for every ζ > 0, so the rest state is asymptotically stable.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear: its one equilibrium does not split.

limitations: Linear spring and damper only; a nonlinear stiffness needs a separate declaration.
One degree of freedom.

acceptance.reference: |H| = 1/√((1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²) (University of Alberta, Vibrations and Sound, equation 5.14); the exact rational A and B for the record.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the steady solution; 1e-6 absolute for RK4 in A and B; 1e-6 relative for the energy balance.
checks: The steady solution satisfies the equation exactly.
The work of the force equals the energy that the damper removes.
RK4 from rest reaches the same steady motion.

solver.method: Closed form for the steady response; RK4 for the transient as a check.
solver.discretization: 200 RK4 steps in each forcing period. The map has 41 × 31 points.
solver.convergence: The transient below 1e-10; the steady parts within 1e-6.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript; rational arithmetic for the exact checks.

declarations.title: Vibration modes of a pinned beam under an axial load

model.summary: A pinned beam of length L, bending stiffness EI and mass m_l per unit length vibrates freely as w = W(x)cos(ωt). An axial compression P lowers the frequencies.
closures: Euler–Bernoulli bending; no shear deformation and no rotary inertia.
model.geometry: A straight beam between two pins at x = 0 and x = L.

conditions.meaning: no deflection at the first support
no bending moment at the first support
no deflection at the second support
no bending moment at the second support

assumptions.text: Euler–Bernoulli beam: no shear deformation and no rotary inertia.
Harmonic free motion w = W(x)cos(ωt).

symbolic: Exact check that sin(nπX) is a mode with Ω² = (nπ)⁴ − λ(nπ)², in rational multiples of powers of π.
numerical: Hermite cubic elements with the consistent mass: K v = Ω² M v on 2 to 32 elements.
SciPy's eigh on the same 8-element matrices as an independent check.

dominant-balance.reason: Every mode balances bending, axial load and inertia together; no term is small.

asymptotic.reason: For a small λ the frequency is Ω₁ ≈ π²(1 − λ/(2π²)); the unloaded frequency is the first term.

stability.reason: Ω₁² = π⁴ − λπ² is positive for λ < π²: the straight beam is stable. At λ = π² the first frequency is 0, the Euler critical load.

bifurcation.reason: The model is linear in W; the zero frequency at λ = π² is the buckling point, and its branch needs the nonlinear model.

limitations: Pinned ends only.
No shear deformation and no rotary inertia (Timoshenko effects need a separate declaration).
No damping.

acceptance.reference: ω_n = (nπ)²√(EI/(m_l L⁴)) for λ = 0 (MIT 16.20, Unit 23); SciPy eigh for the 8-element matrices.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the modes; 1e-4 relative for the first three element eigenvalues on 32 elements; 1e-10 against SciPy.
checks: sin(nπX) satisfies the equation and the four conditions exactly.
At λ = 0 the element eigenvalues on 32 elements are within 1e-4 of (nπ)⁴, and converge at an order above 3.5.
The page's eigenvalues agree with SciPy.

solver.method: Hermite cubic elements, K v = Ω² M v by a Cholesky factor of M and cyclic Jacobi rotations.
solver.discretization: 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 elements.
solver.convergence: Observed order of the eigenvalue error above 3.5.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision.

declarations.title: Simply supported rectangular plate under uniform pressure (Navier)

model.summary: A thin rectangular plate a × b with bending stiffness D carries the uniform pressure p. Its four edges are simply supported.
closures: Kirchhoff plate: D = Eh³/(12(1 − ν²)) and M_x = −D(w_xx + νw_yy).
model.geometry: A rectangle 0 < x < a, 0 < y < b.

assumptions.text: Thin plate (Kirchhoff): normals stay normal, and the deflection is small compared with the thickness.
Simply supported edges: w = 0 and no bending moment on each edge.

symbolic: Exact check of the dimensionless equation and the eight conditions.
Exact check that each Navier term sin(mπX)sin(nπY/β) is an eigenfunction of ∇⁴ that meets the edge conditions.
numerical: The Navier double series at the centre, with its convergence in the number of terms.
Finite differences: two Poisson problems with conjugate gradients, on 8 to 64 cells, as an independent check.

dominant-balance.reason: Bending carries the whole pressure: the linear plate has no membrane term to compare.

asymptotic.reason: For β → ∞ the centre of the plate bends like a strip of width a, W → 5/384; the one-term Navier approximation keeps only the first term of the series.

stability.reason: A plate under lateral pressure has no buckling load; plate buckling under in-plane load needs a separate declaration.

bifurcation.reason: The linear problem has one solution for every pressure.

limitations: Simply supported edges and uniform pressure only.
Small deflection: no membrane stretching (large deflection needs a separate declaration).
No shear deformation (thick plates need a separate declaration).

acceptance.reference: The Navier series; for a square plate the centre coefficient 0.00406 (Kelly, equation 6.5.52). mpmath sums the series to 30 digits (tools/structures_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: 1e-6 relative for the series with odd terms up to 61; 5e-4 relative for finite differences on 64 cells.
checks: Each Navier term meets the operator and the edges exactly.
The series agrees with the mpmath sum.
Finite differences converge to the series at an order near 2 (above 1.8).

solver.method: The Navier double sine series; finite differences with conjugate gradients as a check.
solver.discretization: Odd terms up to 61 in each direction; 8, 16, 32 and 64 cells.
solver.convergence: Series terms fall as 1/(mn(m² + n²)²); conjugate gradients to 1e-13; observed difference order above 1.8.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript in double precision.

declarations.title: Axisymmetric cylindrical shell under internal pressure, clamped end

model.summary: A thin circular cylinder of radius R and wall thickness h carries the internal pressure p. One end is clamped; the plane x = L_s is a plane of symmetry. Bending near the clamped end decays into the membrane state.

roles.meaning: distance to the plane of symmetry

closures: The hoop force is Eh w/R; there is no axial force; D = Eh³/(12(1 − ν²)).
model.geometry: A cylinder of radius R; x along the axis from the clamped end.

conditions.meaning: no radial deflection at the clamped end
no rotation at the clamped end
no rotation on the plane of symmetry
no shear force on the plane of symmetry

parameters.meaning: length to the plane of symmetry over the edge length ℓ

assumptions.text: Thin shell: h is small compared with R.
Axisymmetric load and deflection, and no axial force.

symbolic: Exact check of the dimensionless equation W'''' + W = 1 and the four conditions.
Exact check of the edge solution 1 − e^{−ξ}(cos ξ + sin ξ) in ξ = X/√2, and of β⁴ = Eh/(4R²D) = 3(1 − ν²)/(R²h²).
numerical: The exact finite-length solution from a 4 × 4 linear system.
Finite differences on 50 to 400 intervals as an independent check.

dominant-balance.reason: Bending D w'''' balances the hoop membrane force Eh w/R² over the edge length ℓ ∝ √(Rh); far from the edge the membrane force alone carries the pressure.

asymptotic.reason: The bending zone is a boundary layer that decays as e^{−βx}; for a long cylinder (L̂ → ∞) the semi-infinite edge solution is the limit.

stability.reason: Internal pressure does not buckle the shell; buckling under axial or external load needs a separate declaration.

bifurcation.reason: The linear problem has one solution for every pressure.

limitations: Axisymmetric only, internal pressure, no axial force.
A clamped end and a plane of symmetry only.
Thin shell; no plasticity.

acceptance.reference: The edge solution w = (pR²/(Eh))(1 − e^{−βx}(cos βx + sin βx)) with β⁴ = 3(1 − ν²)/(R²h²), (MIT 2.081J, section 5.1.2), and the edge moment p/(2β²) derived from it.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the edge solution; 5e-4 absolute in W for finite differences on 400 intervals.
checks: The edge solution satisfies W_ξξξξ/4 + W = 1, W(0) = 0 and W'(0) = 0 exactly.
β⁴ has two exact forms that agree.
Finite differences converge at an order near 2 (above 1.8).

solver.method: Exact solution of the linear ODE (a 4 × 4 system); central finite differences with ghost nodes as a check.
solver.discretization: 50, 100, 200 and 400 intervals. The map has 161 points.
solver.convergence: Observed difference order above 1.8.
solver.reproducibility: Plain JavaScript; the growing exponentials are scaled by e^{−ξ_L}.

declarations.title: Heated rod between a wall and an elastic support

model.summary: A rod of length L and area A is fixed to a wall at x = 0 and bears on a spring of stiffness k_s at x = L. A uniform temperature rise ΔT makes it expand; the spring resists the expansion.
closures: Duhamel–Neumann law σ = E(du/dx − αΔT); the temperature field is prescribed (one-way coupling).
model.geometry: A straight rod of constant cross-section; x from the wall.

conditions.meaning: the axial force equals the spring force

parameters.meaning: support stiffness over the axial stiffness EA/L

assumptions.text: Small strains; linear elastic material; properties that do not change with temperature.
The temperature rise is uniform and prescribed: the deformation does not change it.

symbolic: Exact check of the dimensionless equation and conditions.
The exact solution U = X/(1 + κ), σ/(EαΔT) = −κ/(1 + κ), and the energy balance, in rationals.
numerical: The stress and the end movement at each point of the map.

dominant-balance.reason: The support stiffness k_s and the rod stiffness EA/L share the thermal force: κ ≫ 1 gives a fixed end, κ ≪ 1 a free end.

asymptotic.reason: The limits κ → ∞ (fixed ends, σ = −EαΔT) and κ → 0 (free expansion αΔTL) are the first terms of expansions in 1/κ and κ.

stability.reason: The linear rod has one equilibrium. Thermal buckling of the compressed rod needs the column model: compare the rod force EAαΔTκ/(1 + κ) with the critical load of the beams-and-columns family.

bifurcation.reason: The linear problem has one solution for every temperature rise.

limitations: Uniform temperature rise only.
Axial deformation only: buckling under the thermal force needs the column model.
Linear elastic material.

acceptance.reference: Free expansion αΔTL and the stress −EαΔT of a fixed rod (Purdue ME 323); SymPy gives the exact record values (tools/structures_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact (rational arithmetic).
checks: U = X/(1 + κ) satisfies the equation and both conditions exactly.
The strain energy plus the spring energy equals half the work of the thermal force.
The limits κ → ∞ and κ → 0 give the fixed and the free rod.

solver.method: Exact solution in rational arithmetic.
solver.discretization: None. The map has 161 points.
solver.convergence: Not needed: the solution is exact.

Pr ≥ 0.6, the range of the latent-heat correction (8.61). Liquid metals need a separate declaration.

symbolic: The exact groups Π₄, Ga, Ja and Pr in rationals, and the film thickness δ(L)⁴ = 4νk(T_sat − T_w)L/(g(ρ_f − ρ_g)h′_fg) as an exact rational.

The exact latent-energy balance at the bottom: the heat through the wall, (4/3)kΔT L/δ(L), equals h′_fg times the condensate flow g(ρ_f − ρ_g)δ(L)³/(3ν); their ratio is 1 exactly when δ(L)⁴ has its exact value.
The exact constant of the mean Nusselt number: Nu_L = (4/3)L/δ(L) = (2√2/3)Π₄^(1/4), so 0.9428 is 2√2/3 rounded.
numerical: The film thickness by the fourth root, the local and mean heat-transfer coefficients, the heat flow per unit width and the film Reynolds number in IEEE double; the Sadasivan–Lienhard correction against the record's h′_fg.

dominant-balance.reason: In the film, gravity balances viscosity (the parabolic profile) and conduction across the film carries the latent heat of the condensate. Inertia and convection in the film are neglected: their ratio to the kept terms is of order Ja/Pr and Re_c, small in a laminar film.

asymptotic.reason: Nusselt's result is the leading order for Ja → 0. The correction h′_fg brings in the first order in Ja; Sparrow and Gregg's boundary-layer analysis confirms it for Pr ≥ 0.6 (Lienhard and Lienhard, Fig. 8.12).

stability.reason: The film becomes wavy at Re_c ≈ 7 and turbulent at Re_c ≈ 400. These are instabilities of the film flow, and the page treats them as an empirical boundary from data. A stability analysis of the film needs a separate declaration with the full film equations.

bifurcation.reason: The film equation has one solution δ = (4X)^(1/4) in units of its scale, for each set of values. No branch exists.

limitations: Laminar films only: above Re_c = Γ_c/μ ≈ 400 the film is turbulent and the page refuses the result; between 7 and 400 ripples raise h by up to about 20 % above Nusselt's value (Lienhard and Lienhard, Fig. 8.15).
A vertical plane wall; inclined walls, tubes and spheres need the effective gravity of Dhir and Lienhard (eq. 8.63) in a separate declaration.
No vapour shear, no superheated vapour and no noncondensable gas.

acceptance.reference: Lienhard and Lienhard, Example 8.6: water at 1 atm on a strip 30 cm high at 90 °C, liquid properties at 95 °C, h′_fg = 2281 kJ/kg; δ(L) = 0.104 mm, Nu_L = 3846, q = 8.68 × 10⁴ W/m², Q = 26.1 kW per metre of width and ṁ = 0.0114 kg/(m·s).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the groups, δ(L)⁴ and the latent-energy balance; relative 5e-3 against the book's three- and four-digit values.
checks: The latent-energy balance at the bottom of the wall holds exactly.
The film thickness, the Nusselt number, the heat flux and the condensate flow agree with Example 8.6.
The film Reynolds number places the film in its regime, and the page refuses a turbulent film.

solver.method: Closed form: δ = (4X)^(1/4) in units of the declared scale; the fourth root in IEEE double; exact rationals for every group and identity.
solver.discretization: None: the film equation has an exact solution.
solver.convergence: Not applicable: no discretization.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals (BigInt) and IEEE double. No random numbers.

declarations.title: Parallel-flow heat exchanger

model.summary: Steady single-pass exchanger in parallel flow: both streams enter at a = 0 and flow in the same direction. The coordinate a is the heat-transfer area passed by the hot stream. The overall coefficient U_HX and the capacity rates C = ṁc_p are constant, and the exchanger loses no heat to its surroundings.

roles.meaning: heat-transfer area from the hot inlet
capacity rate of the hot stream, the smaller one
capacity rate of the cold stream, the larger one or the same
inlet temperature of the hot stream
inlet temperature of the cold stream
heat flow from the hot stream to the cold stream

closures: The local heat flux between the streams is U_HX(T_h − T_c), with a constant overall coefficient. Each stream changes its enthalpy as C dT, with C = ṁc_p constant (Lienhard and Lienhard, section 3.3; Bannerman, Heat exchanger notes, eqs. 23 to 27).
model.geometry: A single-pass exchanger with total area A. The coordinate a runs from 0 at the hot inlet to A at the hot outlet.

conditions.meaning: the hot stream enters at a = 0
the cold stream enters at a = 0

parameters.meaning: number of transfer units U_HX A/C_min, with the hot stream as the stream of C_min

parameters.label: number of transfer units U_HX A/C_min

assumptions.text: Steady operation. Constant overall coefficient U_HX and constant capacity rates C = ṁc_p, with no phase change in either stream.
No heat loss to the surroundings and no conduction along the flow direction.

The declaration names the hot stream as the stream with the smaller capacity rate (C_h ≤ C_c), so NTU = U_HX A/C_h and 0 ≤ C_r = C_h/C_c ≤ 1. For C_h > C_c, exchange the names of the two streams, or the point lies outside the domain.

symbolic: The exact groups NTU = U_HX A/C_min and C_r = C_min/C_max in rationals, and the exact identity C_h·(dT_h/da) + C_c·(dT_c/da) = 0 of the two equations (the conserved enthalpy flux).
The effectiveness ε = Q̇/(C_min ΔT_in) in closed form, ε = (1 − e^{−(1 + C_r)NTU})/(1 + C_r).
numerical: The temperature profiles θ_h(ξ) and θ_c(ξ) by fourth-order Runge–Kutta on 25, 50, 100 and 200 steps. The effectiveness from each stream, the heat balance and the order of convergence.

dominant-balance.reason: Two terms compete along the exchanger: the change of the stream temperature and the heat exchanged with the other stream. NTU compares them. For NTU ≪ 1 the streams change little; for NTU ≫ 1 the temperature difference between the streams decays to zero.

asymptotic.reason: The single-stream limit C_r → 0 gives ε = 1 − e^{−NTU} for every arrangement. The limit NTU → ∞ gives ε → 1/(1 + C_r), below 1: parallel flow cannot reach the cold inlet temperature.

stability.reason: The declared model is a steady, linear boundary-value problem with one solution for each NTU and C_r. It has no dynamics to destabilize. Flow maldistribution or two-phase instability needs a separate declaration.

bifurcation.reason: The equations are linear in the temperatures, so the solution is unique and changes smoothly with NTU and C_r. No branch can split.

limitations: Constant U_HX and constant capacity rates only: a coefficient that changes along the exchanger, or a stream that condenses or boils, needs a separate declaration.
Single-pass parallel flow only. Shell-and-tube and cross-flow arrangements need their own effectiveness relations.
No fouling and no heat loss: both change U_HX and the heat balance.

acceptance.reference: Lienhard and Lienhard, Example 3.5: C_h = 10 000 W/K, C_c = 20 000 W/K, A = 30 m², U = 500 W/(m²·K), inlets 150 °C and 40 °C give NTU = 1.5, C_r = 0.5, ε = 0.596, Q = 655.6 kW, T_h,out = 84.44 °C and T_c,out = 72.78 °C (the book rounds ε to three digits). Eq. (3.20) for ε.
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the groups and the conservation identity; relative 1e-10 for the Runge–Kutta effectiveness against the closed form at 200 steps; relative 1e-3 against the book's rounded values.
checks: NTU and C_r are exact rationals of the record's values.
The heat lost by the hot stream equals the heat gained by the cold stream: exact for the closed form, and within 1e-12 in the Runge–Kutta solution.
The effectiveness, the heat flow and the outlet temperatures agree with Example 3.5.

solver.method: Closed-form effectiveness; classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta for the profiles.
solver.discretization: Uniform steps in ξ = a/A: 25, 50, 100 and 200 steps.
solver.convergence: The error of the effectiveness against the closed form falls by about 16 for each halving of the step (fourth order), down to rounding.
solver.reproducibility: Exact rationals (BigInt) for the groups; IEEE double for the profiles. No random numbers.

declarations.title: Grey absorbing and emitting slab at a uniform temperature between black walls

model.summary: A plane layer of a grey, absorbing and emitting, non-scattering medium with absorption coefficient κ_a, thickness L and a uniform prescribed temperature T_g lies between two black walls at T_1 and T_2. The radiative-transfer equation along a ray with direction cosine μ is solved exactly for the forward (μ > 0) and backward (μ < 0) intensities.

roles.meaning: π times the intensity toward x > 0
π times the intensity toward x < 0
|cos| of the angle between the ray and the x axis
temperature of wall 2 at x = L
net radiative heat flux into the medium at wall 1

closures: Kirchhoff's law for a grey medium: the emission term is κ_a times the blackbody intensity σT_g⁴/π, and the absorption is κ_a times the intensity. No scattering. The net heat flux is q = 2∫₀¹(i_p − i_m)μ dμ in terms of i = πI, and the angular integrals of e^(−τ/μ) are the exponential integrals E_3 (Beach, Özişik and Siewert, 1971).
model.geometry: A plane layer 0 < x < L, unbounded in y and z, between two parallel black walls.

conditions.meaning: wall 1 is black: it emits σT_1⁴ and reflects nothing

assumptions.text: A grey, non-scattering medium with a uniform and prescribed temperature T_g: the energy equation of the medium is not solved.
Black, diffuse walls at uniform temperatures. All temperatures are absolute temperatures, and the ratios keep the fourth powers.

The Rosseland approximation q = −(16σT³/(3κ_a)) dT/dx needs an optically thick medium, τ ≫ 1 (COMSOL, Rosseland approximation). The page applies it only where its error is within the stated tolerance.

symbolic: The exact groups τ_L, r_1 = T_1/T_g and r_2 = T_2/T_g in rationals; the exact solution of each ray equation, i = σT_g⁴ + (i_wall − σT_g⁴)e^(−κ_a s/μ).
The angular integrals in closed form: the slab emissivity ε_s = 1 − 2E_3(τ_L), the transmissivity 2E_3(τ_L) and the net fluxes at both walls.
numerical: E_n(x) by its series or its continued fraction, to about 1e-15.
An independent check: the net fluxes and the absorbed power from Gauss–Legendre quadrature in μ and x of the exact ray solutions, against the closed form.

dominant-balance.reason: Along a ray, the change of the intensity balances emission minus absorption. τ_L/μ compares the path with the mean free path 1/κ_a. For τ_L ≪ 1 the wall intensities pass almost unchanged (optically thin); for τ_L ≫ 1 the medium emits as a black body at T_g except within a few mean free paths of each wall (optically thick).

asymptotic.reason: Thin limit: ε_s = 2τ_L + O(τ_L² ln τ_L). Thick limit: ε_s = 1 − 2E_3(τ_L), with 2E_3(τ_L) < e^(−τ_L). Rosseland diffusion predicts no net flux inside a uniform medium; the exact flux at the mid-plane is 2E_3(τ_L/2)σ(T_1⁴ − T_2⁴), so the page draws where that error is within the tolerance.

stability.reason: The declared model is linear in the intensities with a prescribed temperature. It has one solution and no dynamics.

bifurcation.reason: Linear model with a unique solution for each τ_L, r_1 and r_2: no branches.

limitations: A prescribed uniform temperature of the medium: radiative equilibrium, or coupling with conduction or convection, needs a separate declaration with the energy equation of the medium.
Grey and non-scattering only; band models of real gases need a separate declaration.
Black walls only; grey walls need the radiosity balance of each wall.

acceptance.reference: Beach, Özişik and Siewert (1971), Table 1, c = 0, black walls (ε_1 = ε_2 = 1): Q_0(0) = 0.1674, 0.7806 and 1.0000 and Q_1*(τ_0) = 0.8326, 0.2194 and 0.0 at τ_0 = 0.1, 1 and 10. These are the slab emissivity 1 − 2E_3(τ_0) and the transmissivity 2E_3(τ_0).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the groups; within half a unit in the last printed digit of the table; relative 1e-10 for the quadrature check.
checks: The page's slab emissivity and transmissivity reproduce Table 1 of Beach, Özişik and Siewert at three optical thicknesses.
The net fluxes from quadrature of the exact ray solutions equal the closed form.
The power that the medium absorbs equals the difference of the net wall fluxes.

solver.method: Exact ray solutions; closed-form angular integrals with E_n; Gauss–Legendre quadrature for the independent check.
solver.discretization: Check: 40 Gauss–Legendre points in μ and 40 in x.
solver.convergence: The quadrature agrees with the closed form to rounding at 40 points; the page shows the agreement at 10, 20 and 40 points.
solver.reproducibility: IEEE double; exact rationals for the groups. No random numbers.

declarations.title: Melting of a half-space: two-phase Stefan model (Neumann)

model.summary: A solid half-space x > 0 starts at the uniform temperature T_i ≤ T_m. At t = 0 the wall x = 0 goes to T_w > T_m, and a liquid layer 0 < x < s(t) grows. Each phase conducts heat with constant properties; both phases have one density; the front x = s(t) is at the melting temperature and moves by the Stefan condition. With T_i = T_m the model is the one-phase Stefan model.

specific heat capacity of the solid
superheat of the wall, T_w − T_m
subcooling of the solid, T_m − T_i
far end of the solid (the declared model takes x_f → ∞)

closures: Fourier conduction in each phase with constant properties. The Stefan condition is the latent-energy balance of the front: the heat that the front receives melts ρℓ ds/dt per unit area (Font, eqs. 2 to 5; Roscani and Tarzia, eq. 3.32 with fractional order 1).
model.geometry: A half-space x > 0 with a plane wall at x = 0. The liquid fills 0 < x < s(t) and the solid fills x > s(t).

conditions.meaning: the liquid is at the melting temperature at the front
the solid is at the melting temperature at the front
the far solid keeps its initial temperature
the liquid layer has zero thickness at t = 0

parameters.meaning: Stefan number of the liquid, c_l(T_w − T_m)/ℓ
Stefan number of the solid, c_s(T_m − T_i)/ℓ
far end of the solid in units of (α_l t_r)^(1/2)

parameters.label: Stefan number of the liquid c_l(T_w − T_m)/ℓ
Stefan number of the solid c_s(T_m − T_i)/ℓ
far end of the solid in units of (α_l t_r)^(1/2)

assumptions.text: Pure conduction in both phases with constant properties, and one density for both phases (no flow from the change of density).
A sharp front at the melting temperature, without supercooling and without a mushy zone.
A half-space: the far end x_f of the solid is far beyond the thermal layer, X_f ≫ 2λ/ν + 8√κ·1, so the similarity solution with x_f → ∞ applies.
Ste_s = 0 (T_i = T_m) gives the one-phase model of Font, whose group β = ℓ/(c(T_f − T_c)) is the reciprocal of the Stefan number used here.

symbolic: The exact groups Ste_l, Ste_s and κ = α_s/α_l in rationals, and the exact reduction of the Stefan condition to the dimensionless form with the factor Ste_l.
The similarity reduction η = x/(2(α_l t)^(1/2)): the erf profiles satisfy the heat equation and both front conditions, and the front condition gives the transcendental equation for λ.
numerical: λ by bisection on the decreasing function F(λ) to the last bit; erf and erfc to about 1e-15.
The latent-energy balance by Simpson quadrature of the profiles, against the closed-form energy input.

An independent transient solution: a front-fixing finite-difference scheme in both phases (backward Euler, central differences), started from a profile that is not the similarity profile, on three meshes.

dominant-balance.reason: The latent heat and the sensible heat compete in the front condition. For Ste_l ≪ 1 the latent heat controls and the liquid profile is nearly linear (quasi-steady); for Ste_l ≫ 1 the sensible heat controls. Ste_s and κ measure how much heat the cold solid takes from the front.

asymptotic.reason: The one-phase small-Stefan limit gives λ² = Ste_l/2 − Ste_l²/6 + O(Ste_l³), the quasi-steady front s² = 2Ste_l α_l t at first order. The page compares it with the exact root.

stability.reason: The declared model is the melting problem with a stable planar front. A supercooled liquid or a solidification front with constitutional supercooling can lose stability: that needs a separate declaration with a curved front.

bifurcation.reason: F(λ) decreases strictly from +∞ to −∞, so the similarity solution is unique for each Ste_l, Ste_s and κ. No branch exists to follow.

limitations: One density for both phases: a change of volume at melting needs a separate declaration with the flow it causes.
A half-space with a fixed wall temperature: a finite slab, a convective wall or a heat flux at the wall breaks the similarity and needs a numerical declaration.
Pure conduction: natural convection in the melt needs a separate declaration.

acceptance.reference: Neumann's similarity solution: Roscani and Tarzia, eqs. (3.28) to (3.31) with fractional order 1; with Ste_s = 0 Font's eq. (8), βπ^(1/2)λ erf(λ)e^(λ²) = 1 with β = 1/Ste_l. An independent root from mpmath (tools/family_references.py).
acceptance.tolerance: Exact for the groups; λ within 1e-12 of mpmath; the latent-energy balance within 1e-9; the transient front within 1e-3 relative on the finest mesh, with second-order convergence.
checks: λ is the root of the transcendental equation and agrees with mpmath.
The energy that enters through the wall equals the latent heat of the melted layer plus the sensible heat of both phases.
An independent transient solution moves the front as s = 2λ(α_l t)^(1/2).

solver.method: Bisection for λ; closed-form similarity profiles; Simpson quadrature for the energy balance; front-fixing finite differences (backward Euler) for the transient check.
solver.discretization: Transient check: 20, 40 and 80 intervals in the liquid and twice as many in the solid, with 2 000, 4 000 and 8 000 steps geometric in time from τ = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ to 1/4 in units of t with X = 2(α_l t)^(1/2).
solver.convergence: The front error falls by about 4 for each halving of the mesh (second order in space); the finest error is the stated tolerance.
solver.reproducibility: IEEE double precision; no random numbers. The reference script tools/family_references.py pins mpmath.
